pairs.evidence: e2e/journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:6 The e2e lane keeps the previous run's database state, and nothing clears it automatically when a run starts. Each spec has to clean up after itself and use run-scoped ids ("persisted in the same dev database"). isolation-lanes requires a lane to inherit nothing from the previous run, with the launcher clearing stale leftovers at startup.

techniques.evidence: e2e/journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:55 Specs compensate for state left by earlier runs and sibling specs using unique run ids and self-cleanup. Workers share one server and one SQLite file, and no startup step resets them.
e2e/journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:22 The keyless journeys drive a production build of the real product from outside, not code as a test imports it.
